description: UK gap analysis vs OECD peers — gap scores, policy attribution and priority matrix
ranking_method: Absolute gap score = |UK value - Best value| / StdDev; ranked descending
priority_matrix_method: Impact (1-10) x Feasibility (1-10); product normalised to /10

policy_credit.attribution_rationale: Ireland's FDI strategy and low corporate tax created sustained above-average growth. While MNC-distorted, the underlying lesson on investment attraction applies.

key_policies.reform: Low corporate tax & FDI strategy (1987–present)
key_policies.description: 12.5% corporate tax rate; IDA Ireland targeted MNC investment; IP-friendly Knowledge Development Box; skilled English-speaking labour.
key_policies.outcome: Ireland hosts EU HQs of Google, Apple, Meta, Pfizer, Medtronic; corporate tax receipts >€24bn (2023); GDP/GNI distortion acknowledged.

key_policies.reform: Post-GFC fiscal consolidation & banking sector restructuring (2010–2015)
key_policies.description: €67bn IMF/EU bailout; NAMA bad bank created; five bank recapitalisations; €30bn fiscal consolidation over 6 years; water charges controversy.
key_policies.outcome: Ireland exited programme 2013 — fastest euro area recovery; primary surplus by 2014; 10yr bond yields normalised by 2015.

key_policies.reform: Housing action plan & childcare investment (2021–present)
key_policies.description: Housing For All plan (2021): 33,000 homes/year target; First Home shared equity; NDP capital investment; National Childcare Scheme expansion.
key_policies.outcome: Housing supply increased (though still insufficient); childcare affordability improved significantly; female labour force participation rising.

policy_credit.secondary_rationale: Korea's broadband & digital infrastructure investment drove structural productivity growth.

secondary_key_policies.description: IMF-supported restructuring of chaebols; bank recapitalisation; NPL resolution; corporate governance reform (boards, minority shareholder rights).
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Korea recovered in two years — fastest post-AFC recovery; fiscal consolidation with surplus by 2000; chaebol leverage reduced.

secondary_key_policies.reform: National pension system and social insurance expansion (1999–2008)
secondary_key_policies.description: Extension of National Pension Scheme to all workers; expansion of employment insurance and industrial accident insurance.
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Social safety net coverage expanded; elderly poverty still high but trending down; pension fund became global sovereign investor.

secondary_key_policies.description: Government-funded national broadband rollout; 'Informatisation' strategy; IT-cluster development in Pangyo.
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Korea became world leader in broadband penetration; ICT sector ~10% of GDP; Samsung/SK Hynix global semiconductor champions.

priority_matrix.impact_justification: Sustained GDP growth above peers raises wages, tax revenues and public service capacity. Each 1pp of additional growth sustains ~£25bn of extra annual output over a decade.
priority_matrix.feasibility_justification: UK structural weaknesses (investment, skills, planning) are well-documented but politically contested. Trade policy post-Brexit limits easy wins. Medium-term supply-side reforms are achievable but slow-acting.

policy_credit.attribution_rationale: Sweden's comprehensive welfare state, free education and progressive taxation have achieved the lowest Gini (0.270) among peers, sustained over decades.

key_policies.reform: 1990s banking & fiscal crisis reforms (1992–1997)
key_policies.description: Bank nationalisation and good-bank/bad-bank resolution; fiscal consolidation of 11% GDP; inflation targeting adopted; pension reform initiated.
key_policies.outcome: Sweden's 'model' crisis resolution — banks sold back to market within years; fiscal surplus by 1997; widely cited as template for Ireland 2010.

key_policies.reform: Notional defined-contribution (NDC) pension reform (1998)
key_policies.description: Replaced PAYG DB pension with income-linked notional accounts + funded premium pension; automatic balancing mechanism links benefits to longevity/growth.
key_policies.outcome: Pension system among most fiscally sustainable in OECD; incentivises longer working lives; model adopted by Norway, Poland, Italy.

key_policies.reform: School voucher system & free school reform (1992–present)
key_policies.description: Universal school choice introduced; public funding follows student to private/municipal schools; significant expansion of independent ('friskola') sector.
key_policies.outcome: Increased parental choice; mixed PISA outcomes (initial gains, later stagnation); ongoing debate on segregation; vocational tracks remain strong.

policy_credit.secondary_rationale: Denmark's 2011 tax reform shifted burden from income to consumption while preserving equity.

secondary_key_policies.description: Extension of flexicurity — easy hiring/firing combined with generous unemployment benefits and active labour market policies (ALMPs).
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Unemployment stayed below 6% even through the Global Financial Crisis; one of the highest employment rates in the OECD.

secondary_key_policies.reform: Pension reform — transition from defined-benefit to DC + mandatory labour market pensions (1987–2010)
secondary_key_policies.description: Gradual shift to funded ATP / occupational pensions; increased private savings rate substantially.
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Pension assets ~200% of GDP; sustainable public finances; reduced pressure on PAYG state pension.

secondary_key_policies.reform: 2011 tax reform — shift from income to consumption taxes
secondary_key_policies.description: Reduced marginal income tax rates; offset by higher environmental and property taxes; revenue-neutral.
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Improved labour supply incentives; Denmark remained highest-taxing OECD country with strong growth.

priority_matrix.impact_justification: Reducing inequality improves health, social trust and intergenerational mobility. Scandinavia shows high welfare and growth are compatible.
priority_matrix.feasibility_justification: Requires sustained redistribution and wage policy changes. Politically divisive. Nordic levels require tax-to-GDP ratios ~10pp above current UK, which faces strong opposition.

secondary_key_policies.outcome: Unemployment fell from ~11% (2005) to ~3% (2019); 'German jobs miracle'; real wage growth initially suppressed but recovered.

secondary_key_policies.description: Solidarity surcharge financed eastern reconstruction; Schuldenbremse (debt brake) constitutionalised from 2009; structural surplus achieved by 2014.
secondary_key_policies.outcome: Eastern productivity convergence (still incomplete); constitutional fiscal discipline; debt fell from ~80% to ~60% GDP pre-pandemic.

priority_matrix.impact_justification: R&D investment has the highest long-run multiplier of any public spending (~3-5x). Closing half the gap to Korea/Germany could add 0.3-0.5pp to trend growth within a decade.
priority_matrix.feasibility_justification: R&D tax credits, Innovate UK grants and the Horizon association re-entry provide concrete levers. Cross-party consensus exists. Industrial Strategy already targets 2.4% GDP by 2027. Feasible but requires sustained funding commitment.

policy_credit.attribution_rationale: Netherlands achieves $75.4 USD PPP/hr through Wassenaar wage-moderation agreements, high capital investment, and a strong vocational training system (MBO/HBO).

key_policies.reform: Wassenaar Agreement legacy & wage moderation framework (2010s)
key_policies.description: Building on 1982 Wassenaar, tripartite wage restraint agreements kept unit labour costs competitive; reinforced during sovereign debt crisis.
key_policies.outcome: Netherlands avoided severe competitiveness losses; maintained current account surplus; export growth.

key_policies.reform: Healthcare system reform — regulated competition (2006)
key_policies.description: Replaced state insurance monopoly with regulated private competition; mandatory universal basic insurance; risk-equalisation fund.
key_policies.outcome: Universal coverage achieved; cost-efficiency improved; widely cited as model for market-based universal healthcare.

key_policies.reform: Housing & pension system reforms (2012–2020)
key_policies.description: Tightening of mortgage interest deduction; introduction of social housing means-testing; gradual pension age increase to 67.
key_policies.outcome: Housing market stabilised after bubble; pension sustainability improved; fiscal consolidation achieved.

priority_matrix.impact_justification: The UK productivity gap (~20-35% below frontier) is the single biggest driver of lower wages and living standards vs peers. Closing it fully would add ~£10,000/yr to median wages.

Requires simultaneous improvement in R&D, skills, management quality, investment and infrastructure. No single lever; long gestation periods. Historically very hard to shift quickly.
